sources.entry: Ghostty - Fast GPU-accelerated terminal emulator. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Ghostty is a fast, native, feature-rich terminal emulator with a SwiftUI macOS app and a GTK Linux app, built on a shared Zig core that also powers the libghostty embeddable library.
summary.what_it_does: Ghostty is a GPU-accelerated terminal emulator that aims to combine speed, modern features, and native UIs. The macOS app is SwiftUI-based with Metal rendering and CoreText font discovery, and supports AppleScript and Apple Shortcuts. The Linux app is built with GTK and integrates with systemd when available. Both platforms support multi-window, tabbing, and splits with tab renaming and coloring. The README says it implements standard and modern terminal sequences, including the Kitty graphics and image protocols, clipboard sequences, and synchronized rendering. The project also ships libghostty, a C-compatible library, with libghostty-vt for parsing terminal sequences and maintaining terminal state. The built-in crash reporter saves reports locally in Sentry envelope format and does not send them anywhere automatically.
use_cases: daily terminal emulator on macOS or Linux
running modern TUI apps with graphics support
embedding a terminal in another application
scripting terminal windows with AppleScript or Shortcuts
how_to_run: See the download page on the Ghostty website
See the documentation on the Ghostty website
Developer setup: see the 'Developing Ghostty' document in the repository
notable: Native macOS SwiftUI app with Metal renderer and AppleScript/Shortcuts support
Linux GTK app with systemd integration (always-on, single-instance windows, cgroup isolation)
libghostty: C and Zig library for embedding terminal functionality, with libghostty-vt usable on macOS, Linux, Windows, and WebAssembly
Multi-threaded design with separate read, write, and render threads per terminal
caveats: libghostty API signatures are still in flux and no version has been tagged yet
Ghostty-only control sequences on the roadmap have not been started
Crash reports are only generated on the next start after a crash and may contain sensitive memory contents
